lessons.title: Le réveil du printemps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe and document spring changes in their environment

opening.activity: Circle time with spring awakening sounds. Play recordings of birds, rain, wind through leaves. Ask 'Qu'est-ce que c'est?' Show spring vocabulary cards with actions: PRINTEMPS (stretch like growing plant), NATURE (open arms wide), OBSERVER (binocular hands).

closing.activity: Spring Gallery Walk. Post observation journals around room. Students walk quietly, looking at each other's spring discoveries. End with group celebration: everyone points outside and shouts 'Bonjour printemps!'

troubleshooting.then: Indoor spring exploration: Use houseplants, spring picture books, or videos of spring scenes. Students can practice vocabulary while pointing to spring elements in pictures.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Noticing buds on trees, new flowers, changing weather, animals returning - encourage daily spring observation walks with family

lessons.title: Collection de trésors naturels
lessons.oneGoal: Students will ethically collect natural materials for art-making

opening.activity: Review spring vocabulary from Lesson 1 with actions. Introduce collecting vocabulary: RAMASSER (picking up gesture), FEUILLE (hold up leaf shape with hands), FLEUR (cup hands like flower). Practice 'gentle touch' - soft fingers for handling nature.

closing.activity: Treasure Museum. Each student chooses their favorite treasure to share. Hold it up saying 'Mon trésor spécial!' Others respond 'Merci, nature!' Practice vocabulary by describing color, size, or texture of special treasure.

troubleshooting.then: Pre-collected nature materials: Use teacher collection of safe natural items. Students can still practice gentle handling, sorting, and vocabulary with provided materials.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Finding interesting leaves, stones, twigs in their yard or neighborhood - remind them of gentle collection rules at home

lessons.title: Art éphémère dehors
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create temporary art installations outdoors

opening.activity: Introduce 'temporaire' concept: Build a simple block tower, then gently knock it down. Say 'Art temporaire!' Show pictures of sand castles, chalk art, snow sculptures that don't last forever. Practice vocabulary with gestures.

closing.activity: Photo Gallery Review. Look at photos taken of everyone's temporary art. Practice vocabulary: 'Mon art temporaire était dehors!' Celebrate the beauty of creating art that doesn't need to last forever.

troubleshooting.then: Indoor temporary art: Use natural materials to create arrangements on large paper sheets that will later be recycled, emphasizing the temporary nature.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Making patterns with sidewalk chalk that rain will wash away, building sandcastles that waves take away

lessons.title: Land art miniature
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create small-scale land art using natural materials

opening.activity: Show examples of large land art (photos) vs small land art they'll make. Practice vocabulary: PETIT (pinch fingers close), CERCLE (draw circle in air), SPIRALE (spiral finger motion from center out). Use arms for big, fingers for small.

materials: Small natural materials sorted by type

closing.activity: Scale Comparison. Compare their mini land art to photos of large land art. Discuss: 'Grand ou petit?' Practice size vocabulary. Celebrate that small art can be just as beautiful and meaningful as large art.

troubleshooting.then: Tabletop land art: Use natural materials on individual desk spaces, emphasizing small scale and pattern-making vocabulary.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Arranging shells at the beach, making fairy circles with acorns, creating small rock arrangements in gardens

lessons.title: Couleurs de printemps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will match and recreate spring colors in their art

opening.activity: Spring color hunt in classroom. Look around and identify spring colors already present. Practice vocabulary: VERT (point to green items), ROSE (point to pink items), VIOLET (point to purple items). Use color cards to match what students find.

materials: Color matching cards in spring shades

closing.activity: Spring Color Gallery. Display color mixing results and patterns. Students walk around identifying colors: 'Je vois du vert!' Vote on 'most spring-like color' creation. Sing simple color song using spring vocabulary.

troubleshooting.then: Indoor spring color exploration: Use magazines, colored paper, or picture books to identify and sort spring colors by vocabulary words.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Noticing new green grass, pink blossoms, purple crocuses on walks with family - creating a home color collection

lessons.title: Textures naturelles
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore and recreate natural textures in their artwork

opening.activity: Texture mystery box: Students feel different natural textures (bark, smooth stone, soft moss) without looking. Describe what they feel. Introduce vocabulary: TEXTURE (run fingers across palm), RUGUEUX (rough scratching motion), LISSE (smooth stroking motion).

materials: Collection bags for safe texture samples

closing.activity: Texture Museum. Display texture rubbings and samples. Students touch and identify: 'Cette texture est rugueuse!' Visitors (other students) can feel and guess textures. End with texture vocabulary song.

troubleshooting.then: Indoor texture exploration: Use classroom materials (sandpaper, fabric, plastic) and houseplants to practice texture vocabulary and create rubbings.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Feeling tree bark, smooth stones, soft moss, prickly pine cones - creating texture collections at home

lessons.title: Empreintes de nature
lessons.oneGoal: Students will make prints and rubbings from natural objects

opening.activity: Show handprints and footprints as examples of 'empreintes.' Press hands in playdough, then lift to show print left behind. Introduce vocabulary: EMPREINTE (press hand then lift), FROTTER (rubbing motion), PAPIER (hold up paper sheets).

materials: Paint pads or shallow paint dishes

closing.activity: Print Gallery and Detective Game. Display prints around room. Students try to guess which natural object made each print. Point to print saying 'Cette empreinte vient de...' Celebrate successful detective work.

troubleshooting.then: Classroom object printing: Use textured classroom materials (sponges, textured blocks, stamps) to practice printing vocabulary and techniques.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Making leaf rubbings like they might do on nature walks with family, noticing animal tracks in mud or sand

lessons.title: Jardin artistique
lessons.oneGoal: Students will design and create a small artistic garden space

opening.activity: Show pictures of different gardens: vegetable gardens, flower gardens, artistic gardens with patterns. Discuss what makes a garden 'artistic.' Introduce vocabulary: JARDIN (sweeping arm gesture), PLANTER (digging and placing motion), GRANDIR (start small, grow tall with arms).

closing.activity: Garden Gallery. Display mini gardens and design plans. Students explain their artistic choices: 'J'ai planté comme ça parce que...' Set up observation schedule to watch gardens grow over coming weeks.

troubleshooting.then: Paper garden art: Create artistic garden designs using colored paper, stickers, or drawings, discussing how real gardens could be designed artistically.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Helping with family garden, choosing flowers for beauty and growth, creating mini gardens at home

lessons.title: Mobile de printemps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create hanging mobiles using collected natural materials

opening.activity: Demonstrate balance with simple balance scale or seesaw motion with arms. Show mobile examples moving in air currents. Introduce vocabulary: SUSPENDU (hang finger from other finger), ÉQUILIBRE (balance arms like scale), MOUVEMENT (gentle swaying motion).

materials: Collected natural materials from previous lessons

closing.activity: Mobile Exhibition. Hang all mobiles in classroom where they can move freely. Students observe each other's work, describing what they see: 'Ce mobile a du mouvement!' Test different ways to create gentle movement.

troubleshooting.then: Paper mobiles: Create mobiles using paper cutouts of natural shapes, focusing on balance and movement concepts without fragile natural materials.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Wind chimes on porches, things hanging from trees in wind, watching leaves and flowers move in breeze

lessons.title: Photographie nature
lessons.oneGoal: Students will document nature art through simple photography techniques

opening.activity: Look at photos of nature art from previous lessons. Discuss what makes a good photo vs bad photo. Introduce vocabulary: PHOTOGRAPHIER (camera holding gesture), ANGLE (tilt head/hands different ways), LUMIÈRE (point to light sources).

materials: Previously created nature art or materials for new art

closing.activity: Photography Exhibition Planning. Choose best photos for class exhibition. Practice describing photos using vocabulary: 'J'ai photographié avec cette lumière...' Plan how to share photos with families.

troubleshooting.then: Photography planning: Without cameras, use viewfinder frames to 'frame' shots and discuss angles and lighting, planning future photography sessions.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Taking pictures of their gardens, pets, special places outdoors - sharing nature photos with family

lessons.title: Art avec les saisons
lessons.oneGoal: Students will plan art projects that change with seasonal cycles

opening.activity: Review four seasons with pictures and actions. Discuss how nature changes through seasons. Introduce vocabulary: CYCLE (circular motion with arms), CHANGEMENT (transform gestures from one thing to another), SAISON (hold up 4 fingers, name each season).

materials: Art materials for current season documentation

closing.activity: Seasonal Art Calendar. Create simple calendar marking when to check seasonal art projects. Practice vocabulary: 'Le cycle des saisons change mon art!' Set reminders for future observations.

troubleshooting.then: Seasonal art comparison: Use photos and examples to compare how the same art project would look different in each season, discussing vocabulary without long-term planning.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Watching their planted gardens grow, trees change through year, creating seasonal decorations at home

lessons.title: Installation collaborative
lessons.oneGoal: Students will work together to create a large environmental art installation

opening.activity: Review smaller art projects from previous lessons. Discuss working together: what works well, what's challenging. Introduce vocabulary: ENSEMBLE (link arms with classmates), GRAND (stretch arms wide), COLLABORATION (shake hands, work together gestures).

materials: Tools for arrangement (rakes, shovels if needed)

closing.activity: Installation Celebration. Gather around completed installation. Each student says one word describing the collaboration: 'Magnifique!' 'Ensemble!' 'Grand!' Plan how to share installation with school community.

troubleshooting.then: Classroom collaborative installation: Create large-scale art installation indoors using collected natural materials, focusing on teamwork and vocabulary.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Working with neighbors on community gardens, school beautification projects, family art projects

lessons.title: Respect pour l'environnement
lessons.oneGoal: Students will demonstrate understanding of environmental responsibility in art

opening.activity: Discuss how they've used nature in their art. What happened to natural materials? What stayed in nature? Introduce vocabulary: RESPECTER (gentle handling gesture), PROTÉGER (sheltering arms), RESPONSABLE (point to self, responsible gesture).

materials: Materials for minor restoration (seeds, small plants, cleanup supplies)

closing.activity: Environmental Promise. Students make personal promises about how they'll be responsible environmental artists. Share promises: 'Je promets de respecter...' Create display of class environmental art guidelines.

troubleshooting.then: Environmental art ethics discussion: Use photos and scenarios to discuss responsible environmental art practices without outdoor assessment.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Leaving nature spaces better than they found them, teaching family members about environmental responsibility

lessons.title: Art et météo
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create art that responds to or incorporates weather conditions

opening.activity: Check current weather conditions. Act out different weather: PLUIE (finger rain), SOLEIL (arms in circle overhead), VENT (swaying motion). Discuss how weather affects outdoor art. What art works in each weather?

materials: Weather-appropriate art materials (water-soluble paints for rain, light materials for wind, etc.)

closing.activity: Weather Art Documentation. Photograph art with weather conditions visible. Discuss how weather helped or challenged art-making. Practice vocabulary: 'Avec la pluie, mon art...' Plan weather art for different seasons.

troubleshooting.then: Indoor weather art: Simulate weather conditions indoors (spray bottles for rain, fans for wind, lamps for sun) and practice weather vocabulary with art-making.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Puddle jumping, shadow play, flying kites, catching snowflakes - weather as natural art partner

lessons.title: Expo nature printemps
lessons.oneGoal: Students will curate and present their environmental art collection

opening.activity: Review all environmental art created during unit. Look at photos, saved examples, documentation. Discuss what exhibition means. Introduce vocabulary: EXPOSITION (gesture showing display), PRÉSENTER (formal showing gesture), PARTAGER (giving/sharing motion).

materials: All documentation and preserved work from unit

closing.activity: Exhibition Opening. Invite other classes or family members if possible. Students present their work: 'Voici mon art environnemental!' Practice vocabulary while sharing. Celebrate growth and learning throughout unit.

troubleshooting.then: Virtual exhibition: Create digital exhibition using photos and recordings of student presentations, focusing on vocabulary use and reflection.

lessons.realWorldConnection: Sharing nature discoveries with family, creating outdoor displays at home, continuing environmental art exploration

familyConnections.unitLetter:
Chers parents et familles,

Nous sommes ravis de commencer notre nouvelle unité: ""

Cette unité permettra à votre enfant de:
• Explorer des concepts importants en arts visuels
• Développer du vocabulaire en français
• Pratiquer de nouvelles compétences
• Faire des connexions avec la vie quotidienne

Quelques thèmes que nous explorerons:
Le réveil du printemps, Collection de trésors naturels, Art éphémère dehors, Land art miniature, Couleurs de printemps

Comment vous pouvez aider à la maison:
• Demandez à votre enfant de partager ce qu'il/elle a appris
• Pratiquez le nouveau vocabulaire ensemble (voir la liste ci-jointe)
• Essayez les activités suggérées quand vous avez du temps
• Célébrez les efforts et les progrès, pas seulement les résultats

Valorisez le processus créatif autant que le produit final.

N'hésitez pas à me contacter si vous avez des questions ou si vous souhaitez partager des ressources culturelles liées à cette unité.

La créativité s'épanouit avec votre encouragement!

Cordialement,
[Nom de l'enseignant(e)]
